scope: Fictional injected current-owner call/slot facts. Labels denote opaque objects constructed by a later closed test harness, never serialized production authority or a measured C execution history.
ordinary_types: All integer fields require exact int, never bool; flags exact bool; arrays exact list at fixture boundary; reference/enum strings exact finite grammar. No executable snippets, open paths, caller checker functions or arbitrary field sets.

tags.UNOBSERVED: value must be null; harness decodes to one dedicated private sentinel object, not None or0
tags.NULL: value null; explicitly OBSERVED null pointer, distinct from sentinel and not guessed failure ownership
tags.HANDLE: strict uint64 including0 and18446744073709551615; function-specific interpretation
tags.BOOL32: strict signed32 raw BOOL; nonzero is success, no bool normalization of the stored fact
tags.COUNT32: strict uint32 observed count cell; observation alone does not mean count-defined

first_fact_atom.sole_authority: A stored atom other than UNOBSERVED is the first observed value fact. scalar_aux_ack/count_aux_ack/right_transfer_ack may remain false; neither a later flag nor a multi-field transaction is required to preserve the value. Reconciliation derives facts from the field/sentinel, not auxiliary flags.
first_fact_atom.count_defined: For ReadFile/WriteFile ONLY: stored raw BOOL32 nonzero, count atom COUNT32, and0<=count<=the predeclared request. UNOBSERVED count, failed BOOL, or out-of-range count is not defined. A COUNT32 value0 sampled from initialized storage with false BOOL is observed but not defined; successful/defined0 is a distinct known zero. Before wrapper stop, an unobserved count may be pending rather than finally unknown; later first count observation may resolve it.
first_fact_atom.residual_window: No fixture claims observation between C return and Python conversion/first storage. An invocation whose scalar field remains UNOBSERVED has an unknown return/effect, even if C might have returned. Preallocation does not establish atomicity.

namespace_state_rule: Exact{scope,owner_ref,output_ref,namespace_owned,reservation_ready}; scope HARNESS_ONLY, refs exact current owner/output identities, flags strictbool and readiness implies ownership. These describe preexisting state of the same typed fictional owner, not a dict/producer ready token accepted by the adopter or production engine. Ordinary raw-only fixtures start false/false; preexisting early-context handoff fixtures start true/true and MUST preserve them. No new namespace/output reservation is inferred or executed.
defined_zero_scope: A successful defined count0 is a known zero raw result and may complete this adoption primitive. Requested3 is only an upper bound; this raw schema has no FileSpec remaining-length proof. Unexpected EOF, whole-file hash/capture and write-progress completeness remain separate b778/source/owner gates, not inferred from the request.
identity_prefix_rule: Exactly empty list or one HARNESS_ONLY descriptor{slot_ref,query_names,scope}, query_names exactly GetFileType/GetFileInformationByHandleEx/GetFinalPathNameByHandleW in order. This declares a typed fictional three-query precondition solely to isolate the fourth return boundary; it is not a completed identity capability and grants no content I/O or production authority.
initial_objects: List of exact{id,kind,scope}; id ASCII[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,31}, unique. kind owner/origin/nonce/registry/port/output/source_context/loader/journal/file_identity/buffer/exception. scope HARNESS_ONLY. Different labels MUST produce distinct opaque object identity even when numeric starts or bytes agree.
reference_rules: current and every handoff.refs have exactly current_exact_keys. Each nonnull ID must exist and have its matching kind; unknown/wrong-kind refs reject before mutation. Only early_context may be null when initial.early_context is null, and that setup cannot satisfy a handoff. Object labels are lookup instructions for typed HARNESS_ONLY objects, not themselves capabilities.
clock_rules: Source-issued original object, start0/work295000000000/hard300000000000 in these fixtures. Steps advance monotonically, never reset. The numeric values are synthetic data, not sufficient owner identity or a live first-clock guarantee.
slot_rule: Any initial usable file/search handle and identity capability is an explicit HARNESS_ONLY precondition tied to its actual typed owner/nonce/slot. Production must not accept this descriptor, HarnessIdentityPrecondition, a dict or an identity_ok flag as proof. Empty open-target slots start UNOBSERVED/no close right.
buffer_rule: Closed fake buffer object, generation0..3, canonical lowercase even hex<=capacity. A reserved call retains the exact object+generation before invocation. Raw fake writes may populate it before scalar storage; no reuse while returned bytes remain uncopied/unhashed or an operation failed. No reported path/file is read.
exception_rule: Harness constructs ONE exception object per ref before the trace; future pure tests compare original object identity, not just class/message. An already latched primary is never replaced by wrapper/close/publication errors.
early_context_rule: Either null (no early-source precondition and no possible handoff) or an exact early_context object. A nonnull object describes explicit fictional preexisting live-source capture from the SAME owner/Origin/nonce/registry/port/loader/journal; scope HARNESS_ONLY. Reusing exact objects/immutable bytes and spent time is tested. It is not a source-freshness claim or ready token accepted from JSON. Later closed harness must construct typed context through reviewed injected factory interfaces; production/live/source gates remain pending.
call_record_rule: Preallocate every field before invoke. raw_scalar/raw_count initially UNOBSERVED. No RawReturn/error copy/log/clock/copy/hash is needed to hold a first fact. Fields retain function-specific values when a wrapper later raises. Ordinal belongs to exactly one current owner/API/slot descriptor.

step_rules.reserve: Exactly one reserve per ordinal, even an identical second reserve rejects. The ordinal has one current owner/API/slot descriptor. ReadFile requested is strictint1..65536 and its exact retained buffer has capacity>=requested. WriteFile requested is strictint1..65536 and equals len(prepared_hex)/2; prepared bytes are retained before invoke. Other APIs requested is null. Metadata/search outputs require the exact preallocated capacity from reserved_buffer_domains even for a later failing return; other APIs buffer_ref null. declared_empty is strictbool, false except for explicitly declared FindFirstFileExW empty-directory probes. INVALID+defined error2+declared_empty allows empty; initial error18 is not natural end. No hidden retarget/reset of a record.
step_rules.invoke: At most one invocation reservation per ordinal, after its unique reserve. Repeated invocation rejects before a second dispatch. Conservative reservation uses the original clock/current typed identity and is not proof of actual native entry. Close invocation consumes the single right BEFORE the call; wrong closer or repeated close does not dispatch.
step_rules.scalar_count: A direct first-fact assignment requires that exact ordinal's invocation reservation. Scalar tag must belong to that API and cannot be UNOBSERVED (sentinel is initialization only). Only ReadFile/WriteFile permit count steps; their count field is initially UNOBSERVED or observed COUNT32, and a count step stores COUNT32 only. Conflicting repeated facts reject before changing any prior fact/ownership/contribution. Identical fact writes and reconciliations are idempotent.
step_rules.aux: field is scalar_aux_ack/count_aux_ack/right_transfer_ack only. It is diagnostic bookkeeping, not eligibility or the source of an observed fact.
step_rules.error: After that invocation's scalar is stored, capture an observed DWORD local-error value with strictbool defined. Initial raw_error is UNOBSERVED and error_defined false. Defined true is allowed only on that API's documented failure/unknown return branch (BOOL0, HANDLE INVALID/NULL, or DWORD0), never from a success stale error. Error-copy failure leaves the error field UNOBSERVED without erasing earlier scalar/count/ownership. Conflicting repeated errors reject before mutation. This adds no GetLastError export or actual error-copy operation.
step_rules.raise: ordinal is existing ordinal or null for pure handoff/control stop. phase is from the closed phase enum. Stop future work, preserve raw facts/first primary, permit only declared same-owner reconciliation/once cleanup while hard time allows. No new scalar/count may be supplied to a stopped invocation; only facts already stored may reconcile. A new legal cleanup-close call has its own ordinal and may observe its own result.
step_rules.copy_hash: Pure buffer-copy/hash component actions, not fixture-driven successful counts. A missing/throwing action cannot set a positive captured/hash byte count; exact known raw slice remains retained. Tests later execute real pure helpers with injected failures, not authored expected outcomes.
step_rules.handoff: refs exactly current_exact_keys, known IDs/matching kinds before comparison, then exact same current object identities and nonnull current early context. At most one claim. No new owner/Origin/output reservation, early-source reopen or run_once invocation. Foreign refs fail even if scalar starts/bytes match.
step_rules.clock: No fresh work at/after work_end, no further invocation at/after hard_end. Previously stored facts/buffers survive; cleanup deadline cannot erase known ownership or report a positive pin.

primary_reference_rules: primary_exception_ref names an injected exception object whose identity must be preserved, or null when no injected object is asserted. A semantic guard may still have a source-created primary: primary_code records that closed predicate outcome. Existing injected primary wins over every later error; secondary_exception_refs retain subsequent injected identities in order.
counter_rules: Known scalar/count values are authoritative projections of non-UNOBSERVED fields even before an auxiliary/cached counter is updated. They fold once per current ordinal+field, independent of number/order of reconciliations. unique_reconciled_ordinals counts distinct reconciled records, not field observations. Logical reservations count successfully created call records; a rejected second reserve does not create another record. Wrapper returns count separately. These are fictional reserved/observed axes, not a measured C-entry/callee-execution census. No resetting earlier known counts during continuation.
incremental_fold: Projection derives known scalar/count values directly from non-UNOBSERVED atoms even before aux/reconcile. Reconciliation tracks each ordinal AND its field-level contribution watermarks: scalar-known then later count-known has one unique ordinal, one scalar return and one count-value contribution, and may advance known bytes once. Never skip a later first count because the ordinal was seen; never double count an identical fact. Pending resolves when count is observed; a wrapper stop with missing/undefined data remains final unknown. This is not a measured C-entry census.
close_success_rules: Exact null|strictbool. Unattempted or invoked-unobserved close is null; never fabricate false. For an observed BOOL32 closer, success is (raw!=0), independent of aux flag/wrapper return. closed_known=>true, close_failed_known=>false, close_return_unknown=>null. At most one closer invocation per slot, including false/unknown outcomes. The stored handle fact remains audit data after right consumption.
buffer_transition_rules: buffer_write must name an existing retained object and exactly current strict generation0..3; canonical even hex length<=its capacity. Reuse requires no pending/failed/uncopied/unhashed retained call referring to the old generation, new_generation==old+1<=3 and bytes<=capacity. All checks occur before buffer/generation mutation; a rejected reuse preserves old bytes/ref/generation.
checkpoint_rule: Each exact{after_step,projection} is an authored read-only before/after-fault expectation. Projection keys use this schema's exact expected-record/slot/counter field paths. A future harness compares them; they never steer implementation behavior.
